input.recap: The Preferences confusion comes from the JusPrin sign-up card being drawn on both the Account page and the AI page. I wrote up a proposal that splits them and renames AI to "Your own AI". No code is changed yet.
input.ask: Should the "Set up AI" buttons open the Account page once AI becomes "Your own AI"?

content.text:
The confusion has a simple cause: the same "JusPrin account" sign-up card appears on both pages. In [Preferences.tsx:309](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:309) the Account page draws it, and in [Preferences.tsx:340](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:340) the AI page draws it again, above your own API keys and AI apps. So someone who opens either page sees the JusPrin offer first, and the two pages look like they do the same job.

The card is on the AI page because of an earlier decision (2026-10-23, noted at the top of the file). Every "set up the AI" button in the app opens the AI page, so that page had to offer every way to get AI, including signing up. There are three of these buttons: the chat's "not set up" pane, the setup bar, and the composer's configure link ([App.tsx:331](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:331)).

**This is a proposal. Nothing is changed yet.**

1. In the sidebar, keep "Account". Rename "AI" to **"Your own AI"** and give it a key icon instead of the robot. This matches the "Your own API key" heading the page already uses.
2. The "Your own AI" page drops the JusPrin sign-up card. Its intro becomes: "Use AI you already pay for: an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or an AI app like Claude or ChatGPT. No JusPrin account needed." A single line at the bottom points the other way: "Prefer JusPrin's built-in AI? Sign up in Account."
3. The "New chats start with" model picker stays on "Your own AI". It only matters once you have more than one way to get AI, and the people who have that are the ones using their own keys.
4. The privacy note at the bottom of the AI page gets split. The sentence about JusPrin passing your messages on to its model provider moves to Account. The sentence about your own provider stays on "Your own AI".
5. Account doesn't change. It already ends with "Your own API key or AI tool works without one", which links to the other page.

**Decision needed: where should the "set up the AI" buttons go once the AI page only covers your own AI?**

This is your call because it reverses the 2026-10-23 decision, and it decides what a brand-new user sees first. There are two options:

- **Open the Account page (my pick).** A new user lands on the JusPrin sign-up card, with the "use your own key instead" link right below it. It costs one extra click for people who bring their own key.
- **Keep opening "Your own AI".** People who bring their own key get there directly. But a new user lands on a page full of API key fields, and the JusPrin offer is now just one line at the bottom. That probably means fewer JusPrin sign-ups.

Should the "set up the AI" buttons open the Account page?

Once you answer, I'll make the change in the JusPrin repo. It's on the `jusprin-newui` branch, which has some untracked notes in it. I'll update the Preferences tests that check the "AI" label and the duplicate account row, and then check both pages in the running app.

Yes, the card was still there last round. I'd left it because removing it depended on where the "Set up AI" buttons go. I took your question as a yes and made both changes. The work is on `jusprin-newui-integration` in `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/byoai`, and nothing is committed.

## BYOAI without the JusPrin account

**The BYOAI page** no longer shows the JusPrin sign-up or sign-in card (screenshot sent):
- The intro reads: "Bring Your Own AI: an API key or an AI app you already pay for. No JusPrin account needed."
- A line at the bottom says "Rather use JusPrin's own AI? Sign up in Account". It's hidden once you're signed in.
- The privacy note at the bottom covers only your own provider now.

**The Account page** gets the sentence that used to sit on BYOAI: with a JusPrin account, JusPrin receives your messages and passes them to the model provider it uses.

**The "Set up AI" buttons now open Account instead of BYOAI.** Otherwise new users would never see the sign-up offer. This affects:
- the chat's "not set up" pane, its setup bar and the composer's configure link
- the printer chat's "Set up AI" button
- the "Set up" button on print-issue bubbles in the 3D view
- the calibration prompt when no AI is set up

The first-launch "use your own AI account" card still opens BYOAI, since that one is specifically about your own key.

**Testing:**
- The type-check and all 692 Agent UI tests pass. Four of those tests changed to expect Account.
- I rendered both pages with the real stylesheet and checked them by eye.
- **Not run:** the native C++ change (two lines in `ShellController.cpp`) and the three shell-harness checks I updated to expect Account. Running them means building JusPrin from this new worktree, which has no build folder yet.

## The last two commits on `jusprin-newui`

**My recommendation is not to squash them.** They overlap but aren't one task, and squashing would break the shared history.

- **They overlap, but they aren't one task.** `b0a2fe3b08` (Nov 6) is the first launch and the new File › Import from OrcaSlicer window. `d7975301fd` (Nov 7) does revise some of that work. It rewrites the sign-up offer wording and removes the import Retry button that the Nov 6 commit added. The two commits touch 41 of the same files. But most of the Nov 7 commit is unrelated: the server-filled Account box, the app-wide "AI" wording sweep, G-code hashes leaving the print history, the OrcaSlicer cloud-login keychain fix, and the design-guidelines doc.
- **Squashing would rewrite history other branches build on.** `b0a2fe3b08` is already pushed, and `origin/jusprin-newui` points at it. `jusprin-newui-integration` is built on top of it too. Squashing would need a force-push to `jusprin-newui` and would make it diverge from the integration branch. The Nov 7 commit is local only and is itself a squash of integration commits.
- **One combined commit would be about 120 files.** It would carry two long, separate messages, and you could no longer revert the first-launch work apart from the wording sweep.
